answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Reaching the comet of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Work waits on the basalt until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the forge of the next round. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool.
